The migration itself went fine, and shockingly fast, taking only 40 seconds this time (six last time, no clue as to why the discrepancy). I did have to restart the cache warmer halfway through, since it doesn't block on the migration lock and I ended up with a partially warm index, and I could see this because p99 latency spiked to ~900ms for about a minute before evening out. In the future I'll have the warmer block on the lock too; less sexy, but also I didn't get paged so I'm all for it.

There's still the issue that the credit count refreshes on a UTC boundary so a run that begins at 23:58 UTC may exhaust its credit allotment two minutes in to execution. I've added a comment to the relevant trace but haven't addressed it in any more substantial way, and since we optimistically debit the estimated cost when adding a job to the queue the worst that could happen is reporting inaccurate (too high) credit usage for a particular day until we're able to recalculate once results are in.

Also should review Sasha's PR adding jitter to retries sometime tomorrow (assuming the filesystem the queue is on cooperates).

At some point after Friday's rollout I should also prune some of the longer test texts, as many of them feel padded because they are. First I need to figure out why we keep accruing thousands of stale tmp files on staging.
